First slice of #1442: lathe chucks generated as built-in fixture accessories.

- `camcraft_sim::chuck` (new): `JawChuck` (body diameter/length, through bore, grip diameter, jaw length/width/height) and `ColletChuck` (body, nose diameter/length, collet bore). Each builds closed steel shells (body annulus + 2..12 jaws, or nose over body) and validates its figures by name: non-finite, zero, negative or absurd sizes, a bore past the body, jaws reaching past the body or meeting each other, a collet bore past the nose, a nose wider than the body.

- New placement `AccessoryPlacement::OnStock` (`accessory::chuck::fit_to_stock`): closes the chuck on the setup's round stock on its axis (jaw face at the stock's underside; a collet the nose length deeper). Square stock, no stock, or a non-chuck kind is refused by name.
- MCP `add_accessory`: the chuck kinds, their dimensions in the schema, and a `fit_to_stock` flag.
- The UI dialog lists the new kinds through `accessory::KINDS` and places them by pose (no UI code change).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/1442-lathe-chuck-fixtures.md` (frame, conservative facetting, no mill refusal, chucks not `fixed`).

title: fix(setups): re-applied two-axis part picks refuse as already held
body:
## What changed

`pick::align_from_axes` (#769, both +Y and +X picked) re-composed an identity turn about the part centre onto the held alignment, which left float noise in the origin (e.g. y `-7.499999999999999` vs `-7.5`). `change_of` compares exactly, so re-applying the same picks stored a no-op undo step instead of refusing.

Now a turn below a quarter of the landing tolerance (`LAND_TOL / 4` = 2.5e-10 rad) hands back the held alignment unchanged, and `AlignPartToSetup` refuses "setup '...' already holds the part that way". The GUI (Setups page "Part axes" Apply, through `check_align` / `align_from_axes`) and MCP `set_part_axes` share that path, so both get the same refusal. The landing proof still runs on the returned alignment. A real turn is built and stored exactly as before; `change_of`, the undo history for real changes and the WCS are untouched.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1347-noop-part-picks.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests. Both failed on the old code (checked by reverting `axis.rs`):
- `crates/app/tests/align_axes_reapply.rs::re_applying_the_same_two_axis_picks_refuses_as_already_held`: the command and `check_align` refuse by name, nothing is written, and one undo is as modelled.
- `crates/app/tests/align_axes_reapply.rs::a_real_further_turn_from_the_held_alignment_still_goes_through`: a different pick from the held state is still one undo step, and undo restores the held alignment exactly.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_align_axes.rs::set_part_axes_again_with_the_same_picks_refuses_as_already_held`: MCP refuses by name and adds no undo step.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green (app lib, align_axes, align_axes_reapply, axis_align, centre_pick, mcp_align_axes). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests --lib -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI was not launched. The Setups page's Apply greying goes through the same `check_align`, which is pinned headlessly.
- The one-axis in-plane path (`turn_in_plane`) was not changed. It already snaps to exact quarter turns.

Changelog: Re-applying the same +Y/+X part-axis picks now refuses "already holds the part that way" instead of adding a no-op undo step (GUI and MCP `set_part_axes`).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1347

title: feat(kernel): read a Solidcraft design's cached final body
body:
First part of issue 1456: the kernel-side reader for Solidcraft `.sc` designs. The app wiring is not in this PR (see "Not in this PR").

## What changed
- `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft::import_solidcraft(k, bytes, stop)` reads a `.sc` container and returns the cached **final body** as the same checked solidcore `StepSolid` the STEP reader hands out (mm, closed, positive volume), plus the design name, units and the writing app's version. It does not read parameters, sketches or feature history.
- It reads only a cache that is provably this document's: `solidcraft-container/1`, document `solidcraft/<n>` in `mm`, cache format `solidcraft-model-cache/8` (the sample) or `/10` (the published source), producer `solidcraft-truck-adapter/4`, kernel `solidcore`, SHA-256 of `document.json` and of `cache/bodies.bin` both matching the manifest. The final state follows Solidcraft's own published rule (the last feature not skipped).
- Refused by name: empty, not a ZIP, no end record, ZIP64, multi-disk, encrypted, a name listed twice, over 10,000 entries, an entry over its cap (container 4 KiB, manifest 32 MiB, parts 256 MiB), CRC-32 or length mismatch, a directory or data outside the file, an unknown method, an unknown container/document/cache version, another producer or kernel, inch (or any non-mm) units, no model cache, a **stale** cache (the document digest does not match), a payload digest mismatch, slices that overlap, leave gaps, run past or leave trailing data, a body run out of range, no evaluated feature, several bodies, a placed copy (assembly instance), a mesh body (`SCMESH01`), a bad magic, a body that does not decode. Entry names are only compared, never used as paths, and nothing is written to disk. A panic in the decoder or kernel is caught and reported; `stop` bounds the time.
- New modules in `crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/`: `zip.rs` (a bounded in-memory ZIP directory reader written from APPNOTE.TXT), `sha256.rs` (FIPS 180-4, pinned by the standard's vectors), `cache.rs` (the manifest, slices and final state), `mod.rs`. `solidcore_step::build_record` is split out of the STEP reader's `build` so both share the same checks (no behaviour change for STEP).
- Fixture: the maintainer's sample, `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc` (5 MB), marked binary in `.gitattributes`.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1456-solidcraft-import.md`.

## New dependency - needs the maintainer's yes
`camcraft-kernel` gains `flate2 = "1.1"` (deflate for the container) and the workspace's `serde_json`. flate2 1.1.10 is **already in Cargo.lock** (png, tiff, usvg and vtkio pull it), so nothing new is downloaded or built; the lockfile gains two lines (the kernel's two new edges). The `zip` and `sha2` crates were considered and dropped (see the decision file). No new `camcraft-*` edge.

## How tested
- `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_import.rs` (Gate map: covers `camcraft_kernel::solidcraft`), 7 tests, all green in debug (~41 s):
  - `sample_imports_its_final_body_at_the_design_size`: body "Body1", design name, mm, volume > 0, and the exact box equals the design's parameters (d1 = 125 mm diameter, d2 = 85 mm height): [-62.5, 62.5] x [-62.5, 62.5] x [0, 85] within 1e-6; the stored-ZIP rebuild of the same parts imports too.
  - `not_a_container_is_refused`, `container_damage_is_refused`, `documents_we_cannot_read_are_refused`, `a_cache_that_is_not_this_documents_is_refused`, `a_bad_body_table_or_body_is_refused`: one corrupted copy per refusal above, built in the test, each asserting its message.
  - `damaged_files_never_panic_or_hang`: 48 seeded byte-mutations/truncations of the sample plus 16 manifest-text mutations, under a 120 s cancel bound: no panic, no hang.
- `solidcraft::sha256` unit test (FIPS vectors and padding edges).
- Unchanged STEP suites re-run for the `build_record` split: `step_import`, `corrupt_input`, `machining_mesh` - green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick` falls back to the whole workspace for a `Cargo.toml` change and does not include camcraft-kernel; I ran the kernel suites above instead (the only crate touched).

## Not in this PR / not exercised
- **No app wiring**: Model > Open filter, drag-and-drop list and the MCP tool. No crate depends on `camcraft-kernel` yet (the app imports through truck until 917 lands); the first app -> kernel edge belongs there. So nothing is reachable from the GUI or MCP, and there was **no hand test in the app**.
- **Finding, filed as 1463**: the machining mesh refuses this body at every chord tried (0.005-0.1 mm; deviation about 2.8x the tolerance). The refusal is the safe outcome, but the body cannot be machined until that is fixed, so the app wiring should wait for it or show that refusal.
- Multi-body designs, assembly instances, mesh bodies, non-mm designs and cache formats other than 8 and 10 are refused, not read.
- Release-mode and other OSes not run.

Changelog: none (kernel-side reader only, not reachable from the app yet)

body:

A malformed table is refused by name before any hook, only when Explain is on (`Script::explain_refusal` in `js.rs`).

title: fix(turning): a new Facing faces the stock allowance down to the part's top
body:
## What changed

A new lathe Facing, whether created by MCP `add_operation` (`operation::seed_params`) or the GUI quick-add (`quick_params`), took its heights from the mill fold. That gave `top_z` = Top of Model and the facing plane `bottom_z` = Bottom of Model (the #214 floor). `turning::facing` then laddered from z 0 up to the part's top: it cut the part away and never touched the allowance above it.

- `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` `seed_facing`: the seed now states its own heights, the same way it already overrides the stepdown. `top_z` = Top of Stock + 0, and `bottom_z` (the facing plane) = Top of Model + 0. Both new-op paths retype the same Face draft, so both get these heights. Retyping an existing op into a Facing gets them too.
- `crates/app/src/operation/heights_sel.rs` `depth_sane`: a part already at length (stock top == part top) makes the window level. The heights door used to refuse this as "must cut downward: its top height resolves below its bottom height", which is wrong for a level window. A Facing now passes a level window, as Face already does. `generate` then refuses by name: `nothing to face - the facing plane stands at or above the top of both the part and its stock`. This is the generator's existing `GenError::Empty`, so no new status was needed. A top below the plane is still refused by the door.
- `docs/decisions/1409-face-seed-heights.md` records the decision.

The verify wording note from the issue is not changed. The 0.8 mm saturation of `gouge_mm` is shared by every envelope kind, so rewording it is not a trivial change. Verify semantics are untouched.

title: fix(sim): read a turning nose path's hidden rest as the turned work sees it
body:
## What was wrong

A lathe Facing that only faces the end of a bar was refused at the post when the bar had a groove anywhere along it (#1408). The finish-envelope verdict (law f) reported the groove as the Facing's rest. The cause is in the scan's hidden-rest half, which measures every Z-occluded top against the nearest nose centre:

1. **The scan never turned the work.** The groove floor's rim across the spindle, at (-r, 0, z_floor), was read against a path written in the y = 0, x >= 0 meridian. The issue's figures (17.05 / 10.28 / 15.56) are exactly that distance.
2. **Once turned, the near side was still 14 mm below the faced band.** No nose of the Facing travels that far down the spindle.

The Profile half (austin62jake's comment) shares cause 1: 12.49 / 12.76 on the shaft. Once the work turns, two smaller readings remain. Neither is rest the op owes:

- the groove floor's inner corner, which a 0.8 nose cannot reach (0.33 mm, `r(sqrt2 - 1)`);
- the Profile Rough's own 0.25 leave on the groove floor (0.287 on the shaft; 1.06 on the 2 mm near-top groove, which the rough plus its leave cannot enter).

The visible (ridge) half already lets both stand. They reached the hidden half only through Z-occlusion, and Z-occlusion means nothing to a tool that comes in radially.

## The fix

- `VerifyContext::lathe_axis` (new, default `None`): the spindle a turning nose op's kernel fitted. `operation::turning_axis::lathe_axis_of` sets it for every `Family::Turn` op whose tool states a nose radius, by the same `turning::Frame::about` reading the lathe sim uses. A source no axis fits gets `None`.
- `stock_sim::envelope_scan_turned(facets, moves, r, tol, (axis, leave))` (`envelope_scan_centers` is now `(None, 0.0)` of it). Law (f) passes `cx.lathe_axis` and `cx.stock_to_leave` for nose-centre paths.
- `stock_sim::scan_turned` (new, 174 lines) changes only the hidden-rest half, with four clauses:
  1. **The work turns.** Each hidden top is read at itself and at its two turns into the path's meridian plane. Every sample lies on the top's orbit, so the reading can only be at or above the true orbit distance. It may over-read (a refusal) but never hides rest, even on a path that leaves its plane.
  2. **The band.** A top farther along the spindle than every nose centre, by more than the nose plus the scan floor plus the arcs' bulge, is excused.
  3. **The crease.** A top the nose cannot touch is excused. This uses the ridge law's own accessibility test (`ridge::Access::reachable`, the tangent ball along the normal).
  4. **The leave.** A rough's `stock_to_leave` is its promise, and the crease test reads the ball grown by the leave.
- Gouge half, visible half and every mill path are unchanged. Without a spindle the scan is bit for bit the old one; this is pinned.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1408-turned-envelope-hidden-floor.md`. It covers why this is not a switch to `Mode::Revolve` (that is the blade's boxcar law, and the registry already keeps the nose kinds on law f), why the axis is not world Z, and why the hidden half is kept.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/turning_hidden_floor.rs` builds the issue's 64-segment bars on a lathe document with d20 x 50 stock and TN-1600-0R8, and runs them through `posting::post_script` with `fanuc-lathe.cps`:

- `a_facing_over_a_grooved_bar_posts`: groove, groove near the top, shaft. Facing posts.
- `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post`: shaft. Facing, Profile Rough and Profile Finish are clean, and the program is written.
- `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`: groove and groove near the top, with Facing, Rough and Finish.
- `bars_without_a_groove_post_as_before`: plain and stepped post (stepped with Rough and Finish). The bar wider at the free end has no findings.
- `a_facing_that_gouges_the_grooved_bar_still_blocks_by_name`: Facing plane at 47. The `Envelope` warning carries a gouge over 0.5 mm, and the post is refused with "post blocked ... F2 ... finish envelope".

`crates/sim/tests/turned_hidden_rest.rs`:

- `a_groove_floor_under_the_facing_band_is_not_its_rest`: the unturned scan reads more than 15 mm; the turned scan reads at or under the gate; the gouge half is bit-identical.
- `a_hidden_floor_the_nose_could_reach_inside_its_band_still_convicts`: a nose that rides the OD past the 3 mm groove inside its own band reads more than 3 mm of rest, with leave 0 and with leave 0.25.
- `without_a_spindle_the_scan_is_the_old_one_bit_for_bit`
- `law_f_still_blocks_a_real_rest_and_a_real_gouge_by_name`: through `verify` with `lathe_axis` set, both a real rest and a real gouge give a blocking `finish envelope` warning.

Also `scan_turned` unit tests: the band/orbit geometry, and a path on the axis or non-finite.

## Mutation check (standing rule: each new excuse and guard deleted gives RED, restored gives GREEN)

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| M1 delete the band excuse | sim `a_groove_floor_under_the_facing_band_is_not_its_rest`, `law_f_still_blocks_...`; app `a_facing_over_a_grooved_bar_posts`, `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M2 delete the orbit (turned) reading | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M3 delete the nose-accessibility (crease) excuse | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M4 leave not forgiven (`leave = 0.0`) | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| M5 crease test on the bare nose, not nose + leave | app `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves` |
| M6 app passes no spindle (`lathe_axis: None`, i.e. the pre-fix verdict) | app `a_facing_over_a_grooved_bar_posts`, `the_profiles_post_over_both_grooves`, `the_shafts_facing_and_profiles_post` |
| restored | all 4 sim + 5 app tests GREEN |

The two "still blocks" tests are guards against over-excusing: they stay green under every deletion above, by design.

## Goldens

No golden changed. Paths are untouched (only the verdict reads differently), and every app `turning*` and `lathe*` suite passed with a clean tree after it (39 suites, `lathe_post` goldens included).

## Gates

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app` on every `turning*` / `lathe*` suite: 39 suites, all ok.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --test turned_hidden_rest` and `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test turning_hidden_floor`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green, 25.5 min wall (sim 184 s, motion 6 s, app 1209 s, ui 130 s; 0 failed)

## Not exercised

- Boring, Chamfer, Taper and Multi-Pass also get the spindle (same `Family::Turn` + nose door). Their suites pass, but no new fixture puts a groove under them.
- A groove the nose fits but the insert's trailing geometry cannot enter is still judged as reachable. This errs toward refusing.
- The MCP repro was not re-run through `camcraft-cli`. The app tests drive the same commands and the same post gate.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 54); this branch is cut from upstream/main 3f6ecb4a.

Changelog: A lathe Facing (and the Profile kinds) on a grooved bar is no longer refused at the post: the envelope verdict reads hidden floors as the turning work sees them, out-of-band, nose-unreachable and leave-covered tops excused; a real gouge or owed rest in the op's own band still blocks (#1408)

Effort: high (no escalation)

## What changed

`pr-test.yml` is a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow (inputs: PR number, head SHA the reviewer read) that runs a PR's quick gate plus clippy on the maintainer's self-hosted Linux runner, so a review needs no 10-20 GB local worktree.

- Runs only for a PR whose author has push access (maintainer decision "Collaborators only"): the first step checks it through the API and refuses otherwise; other PRs build locally.
- Job targets its own runner label `camcraft-pr-test` (maintainer decision "Separate runner/user"): own OS user, HOME, cargo home and sccache dir, never the cut/release runner of #1413. `CARGO_HOME` and `SCCACHE_DIR` are set under the runner's work dir.
- Refuses a diff touching `build.rs`, `.github/`, `scripts/`, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, a toolchain file, a `.cargo/` directory at any depth, or `xtask/`; the diff is listed with `--no-renames`.
- Checks out `refs/pull/<N>/head`, refuses any head but the SHA given, trial-merges main locally, runs `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` and clippy on touched crates. Read-only token, no secrets, no credentials on disk.
- Actions pinned by commit SHA; artifact retention 7 days.
- PR-reviewer agent, `review-prs` skill and AGENTS.md describe the same rules; decision file `docs/decisions/1420-pr-test-pipeline.md` records both decisions and what was dropped. PROCESS_VERSION 58.

title: fix(slice): section touching or stacked solids as their union
body:
## What changed

`testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` laid flat could not be machined by 3D Finish or 3D Pocket. Both were refused with "invalid machining parameters: chords meet 3+ ways at z = ...: non-manifold contact".

**Cause.** The model is three closed solids. Two of them are stacked so that, laid flat, their cylindrical walls overlap in Z (1.5875 .. 3.175) on the same vertical seam lines. Every plane in that band meets both outlines at the same 93 points, with four chords at each. Those chords run the same way and are subdivided differently, so welding coincident chords would not apply. `slice()` needs exactly two chords per end, so it refused, and `from_slice` reported the refusal as a parameter error.

**Fix** (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice_bodies.rs`, new):
- `slice()` keeps its plain read. Only when that read returns `NonManifold` does it retry as the union of the soup's closed solids:
  - the facets are split into bodies by shared-edge connectivity (corners welded within 0.1 um, spatial hash);
  - the retry runs only when every body is a closed, consistently wound 2-manifold with positive signed volume;
  - each body is then sliced on its own and the sections are united with the 2D boolean union. This is the same law `material_above_of` already applies to bodies from separate entities (M13.11).
- Everything else keeps the refusal:
  - solids welded along a shared edge or face (they share it four ways, so they read as one non-manifold shell);
  - an open body;
  - an inward cavity shell (sliced alone it would read as material, and the union would fill the cavity).
- A mesh that sliced before never reaches the fallback, so every existing CL/G-code golden is untouched by construction.
- The refusal is reworded to name the model and the fix: "the model's surfaces meet 3 or more ways at z = ... (non-manifold contact: solids welded along a shared edge or face, or a shell touching itself) - repair the mesh, or keep each solid a separate closed shell".
- New `GenError::Model`: the app and motion `from_slice` maps send `Open` and `NonManifold` there, so the message reads "the source model cannot be sliced: ..." instead of "invalid machining parameters: ...".
- `material_above_of` and `material_overhead_of` move with the fallback into `slice_bodies.rs` and are re-exported from `slice`. `slice.rs` goes from 466 to 423 lines.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1407-shared-face-slice.md`. Sources: Requicha 1980 (sections of a regularized union), Botsch et al. 2010 (closed oriented 2-manifold test), Zhang & Chen 2001 (signed volume), Teschner et al. 2003 (spatial-hash weld).

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs`
  - `the_sample_laid_flat_generates_3d_finish_and_pocket_with_no_gouge`: the issue's MCP job, laid flat. Both R1 and S1 now report `status: ok`, the program gate (stock sim) is `ok` with no gouge, and every finish-envelope gouge reading is under 0.01 mm.
  - `the_laid_flat_band_sections_as_the_union_of_the_solids`: every plane in z 1.60 .. 3.15 sections, wider than the lower solid alone, and the islands law reads it.
  - `the_sample_as_imported_still_sections_on_the_plain_read`: 240 planes over the as-imported span all slice.
  - `welded_non_manifold_solids_are_refused_as_a_model_fault`: two blocks welded along one edge, through 3D Pocket. Refused with "the source model cannot be sliced ... non-manifold", and never "invalid machining parameters".
  - `the_sample_as_imported_still_generates_both_operations`: `#[ignore]`, heavy lane. The as-imported job spans 118 mm of Z and takes over 15 min in debug.
- `crates/geometry/tests/slice_bodies.rs`: stacked solids, solids touching along a face, welded shared edge still refused (with the new wording), inward cavity shell refused (not filled), open solid refused, nanometre seam drift still welds.
- `crates/motion/tests/islands_model_fault.rs`: `machining3d::material_above` returns `GenError::Model` for the welded soup and the union for stacked solids.

Mutation checks (STANDING RULE). Each line was deleted or changed, the pinning tests went RED, then it was restored and they went GREEN:

| Mutation | RED tests |
|---|---|
| M1: drop the fallback call in `slice()` | stacked, touching, drift (geometry); laid-flat band and laid-flat generate (app) |
| M2: drop the closed/consistent edge guard | `a_soup_with_an_open_solid_is_refused` |
| M3: drop the outward (positive volume) guard | `a_soup_with_an_inward_cavity_shell_is_refused_not_filled` |
| M4: weld tolerance 1e-4 -> 1e-12 mm | `nanometre_seam_drift_still_reads_closed_solids`, laid-flat band, laid-flat generate |
| M5: restore the old refusal wording | `solids_welded_along_a_shared_edge_are_still_refused` |

title: ci: cut pipeline - release gate on a self-hosted Linux runner, then tag and release
body:
## What changed

A **Cut** pipeline that runs the release gate tier on the self-hosted Linux runner and then **triggers the existing `release.yml`** for the tag. It does not replace `release.yml`: that file is unchanged (its jobs, runners and publishing as they are). It already has a `workflow_dispatch` trigger, so not even a trigger had to be added.

- **`.github/workflows/cut.yml`** (new). Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only. Inputs: `version` (X.Y.0), `stage` (`gate` | `tag`) and `dry_run`. Every job is `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`. `concurrency: cut` allows one cut at a time and never cancels a running one.
  - `stage: gate` runs before the release PR merges. It checks out `release/vX.Y.0` with `persist-credentials: false`, so no token is on disk while tests run. It refuses a branch whose `Cargo.toml` or `RELEASE_NOTES.md` doesn't name the version, or whose tag already exists. Then it runs `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots`, inside `xvfb-run -a` when there is no display. It always uploads `gate-logs/` and `gate-output.txt` as an artifact and writes the gate summary to the job summary. When green and not a dry run, it uploads the tested commit as `cut-tip-vX.Y.0`. It tags nothing.
  - `stage: tag` runs after the release PR merged. It finds the newest green gate run for the version and takes its tip. It refuses unless main's head `m` is the release PR's merge of that tip (`m^2 == tip`), `git diff $tip $m` is empty (AGENTS.md step 4's rule, kept), the tag is free on origin and `Cargo.toml` names the version. It then runs `git tag -a vX.Y.0 $m`, pushes the tag, and runs **`gh workflow run release.yml --ref vX.Y.0`** with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A tag pushed with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow by itself; a `workflow_dispatch` from it does. On a tag ref, release.yml's `publish` and `pages` see `refs/tags/...` exactly as they do on a pushed tag. Only this job has `contents: write` and `actions: write`.
  - `dry_run`: the gate stage prints its plan (`--dry-run`); the tag stage runs every check and stops before the tag and the dispatch.
- **xtask**: `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots` is the release plan without the two pixel-snapshot lanes (`--lib --ignored snapshot` and `--test gpu_render --ignored snapshot`). The flag is refused on any other tier. Pinned by `release_without_snapshots_drops_only_the_pixel_lanes`.
- **AGENTS.md**:
  - the release tier entry in the gate tiers list
  - "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted": self-hosted jobs bill nothing, triggers stay `workflow_dispatch`, no fork-triggerable trigger on a self-hosted workflow, and the billed minutes of one cut, with a placeholder to fill in from the first real cut
  - new "The cut runner" section: requirements, registration and safety, written generically with no host-specific names
  - cut steps 2-4 and "Every cut tag is published"
  - the local cut stays as the fallback when the runner is down
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`** 54 -> 55 (process files: AGENTS.md, xtask). The final number is settled at merge.
- **`docs/decisions/1413-cut-pipeline.md`**: the decisions below.

## Open questions settled (details in the decision file)

- **Where the tag is made.** The gate runs on the release branch tip before the release PR merges, so a red gate leaves no untagged release on main. A second dispatch (`stage: tag`) after the merge checks `m^2 == tip` and that `git diff $tip $m` is empty, then tags. The empty-diff rule is kept and is now machine-checked.
- **Windows-only pinned readings** (issue 1402's per-OS move counts). The Linux gate checks only the Linux arm. A local Windows check stays **optional** at a cut, named in step 2. If nobody runs it, the Windows arm drifts until the next Windows run, and the release PR says it was skipped.
- **UI snapshot lane on Linux.** Skipped on Linux (`--no-snapshots`) and kept as a local Windows step at the cut. The goldens are Windows renders, and a GPU-less Mesa render would differ in pixels every cut, or need a second set of goldens kept in step. Their structural twins still run in the ui suites on Linux.
- **Version bump, zip, installer.**
  - The bump stays local on the release branch: `cargo xtask release --version X.Y.0 --no-tag --skip-gate`.
  - `release.yml` already builds the published zip, installer and packages from the tag, and nothing about that changes.
  - The local zip and installer are now a hand-test build only.
  - The installer stays Windows-only, in release.yml's Windows job.

## Runner (already registered)

AGENTS.md lists the requirements generically: Linux x64, labels `self-hosted`/`Linux`/`X64`, disk of at least 100 GB, the toolchain on the service PATH, `git` and `gh`, the build packages from release.yml's linux job, `xvfb` plus Mesa software drivers, and sccache configured in `.env` with no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It also gives the `config.sh` registration and the service setup. **Runner prerequisite to check:** `gh`, `xvfb` and the Mesa and dev packages must be installed on the box. The workflow can't install them, because the runner has no sudo.

## How tested

- `actionlint` 1.7.12 (release binary in a scratch dir, sha256 checked against the release's checksums file, not added to the repo): clean on `cut.yml` and every other workflow. shellcheck was not installed, so the `run:` scripts were not shellchecked.
- YAML parse (Ruby Psych): trigger `workflow_dispatch` only; inputs `version`, `stage`, `dry_run`; jobs `gate` and `tag`, both `[self-hosted, linux]`.
- `cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots --dry-run`: 12 steps, namely every debug suite (kernel included), ui, clippy, and the motion and app heavy lanes, with no snapshot lane.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: xtask unit tests 90 passed, 1 failed. The one failure is `gate_maps_tests::no_gate_map_names_a_moved_module_as_app`, which **already fails on a clean upstream/main 3f6ecb4a** (ten test headers name moved modules as `app::`), so this PR did not cause it. Filed as #1417. With that test skipped, all 90 pass, including `release_without_snapshots_drops_only_the_pixel_lanes`, `batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` and `cli_parses_the_gate_forms`.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No product Rust code changed.

## Not exercised: maintainer's post-merge check

A workflow can only be dispatched once it is on the default branch, so **no real run happened**: not the runner, not xvfb or the UI suites under it, not the artifact hand-off between stages, not the tag push or the release.yml dispatch. After merge, run in this order:

1. `gh workflow run cut.yml -R NeoTech/Camcraft -f version=<test X.Y.0> -f stage=gate -f dry_run=true` checks the runner picks the job up and prints the plan (it needs a `release/v<test>` branch whose Cargo.toml and RELEASE_NOTES.md name the version).
2. The same command without `dry_run` runs the real gate. Expect about 75 min or less. It should prove the UI suites pass under xvfb. A deliberately red commit on the scratch branch should also make no tag (step 3 refuses, since there is no green gate run).
3. After the scratch release PR merges (or on a throwaway fork): `gh workflow run cut.yml -R NeoTech/Camcraft -f version=<test> -f stage=tag -f dry_run=true`, then the same command without `dry_run`. Check that the tag lands on the merge commit and that release.yml starts on the tag and attaches its artifacts to the GitHub release. Then fill in AGENTS.md's "measured cut" placeholder from that run's Usage. Branch protection and tag rulesets must allow `github-actions[bot]` to push tags.

title: fix(sim): the span floor's tilt cap is closed at 90 degrees
body:
## What changed
`crates/sim/src/verify/tilt_span.rs`: `in_cap` now accepts A/B letters at exactly +-90 degrees (`<= 90`, was `< 90`). A span that stays inside the closed cap reads no span floor. Letters past 90 still get #1303's interval floor. The module's law and the decision are written out in `docs/decisions/1404-closed-tilt-cap.md`.

## Culprit
PR #1306 (merge `e74bca1f9`, #1303 tilt-band dip). Release lane bisect: v0.18.0 green, `a0d102834` green, `e74bca1f9` red, current main red.

## Which side was wrong: the check
All 18 hits are blade-lying swarf links that turn B +90 -> -90 with A = C = 0. In the span from the sampled pose B 45 to its neighbour at exactly B 90, the strict cap fell back to the interval bound (`sin_max = 1`), which gives the floor `tip - R`. The turn cells pinned that floor over B 45's footprint, where the band really stands about 34 mm above the tip. Instrumented reading: cell bottoms -3.7 to -5.5 over columns 47 mm out, with the stock top at 9.6 to 11.7.

The dip that floor describes belongs to the horizontal end, and that end's own cells read it in place. On the closed cap, cos A and cos B are >= 0 along the lerp and `ln cos A + ln cos B` is concave, so `cos θ` is smallest at an end (by continuity also where it is 0 there). The ends therefore bound the span. The generator's contact was not real: the cells that follow the actual band positions find nothing once the misplaced floor is gone.

## Readings / tests
- `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test operations -- --ignored swarf`: both full-band tests pass (they were red on main with 18 SweepHits).
- New pin `verify::sweep::tests::a_swing_through_vertical_reads_no_floor_from_its_horizontal_ends`: checks no span floor at any pose, a post 47 mm out topped at +10 is clean, one topped at +40 is still refused, and one under a horizontal end's band (70 mm out, top -2) is still refused. It fails on the strict cap.
- Extended `verify::tilt_span::tests::inside_the_cap_the_samples_bound_the_span_and_past_it_the_floor_does`: 400 brute-force spans with ends at exactly +-90 read `None`, and the lerp never stands under the samples. It fails on the strict cap.
- #1303's pins are unchanged and green (`a_span_past_a_right_angle_...`, `the_backstop_reads_the_exact_dip_lowered_by_the_span_floor`, `tilt_band_dip`, `tilt_tolerance`, `midturn_swept_band`, `midturn_hidden_backstop`).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green (sim 35 s, motion 10 s, app 482 s). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
The rest of the release tier (other heavy lanes, UI snapshots) was not run. That is for the cut.

title: fix(post): floor a capped lathe C-section feed word that rounds over its cap
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, the C-axis live-tool G01 (`liveMove`):

- **#1392, the floored word.** The cap is kept as its own value (`capF`, from #1395's prelude `rotaryFeedCap(Infinity, ...)`), and F goes through `capWord(v, cap)`. It returns `fm(v)` unless that word is over the cap; then it floors the word to the 0.1 step at or under the cap. No tolerance: flooring without one is only ever on the safe side.
- **#1398, posted words.** The cap is measured between the words the control reads. X is read back from its rounded diameter word, Z origin-relative at 0.001, C at 0.001. This is the same rule as `rotaryFeed`'s `q()`/`org` for the mills (#1395). Before, it was measured on the unrounded points, and a short move that rounded longer could drive X/Z about 7% over the maximum feed. The planned F is still scaled by the raw composite length, so feeds away from their cap post byte-identically.
- **F0 refused.** A word under the 0.1 mm/min step is refused by name and not written. One refusal covers a machine-rate cap that floors to F0, another a planned feed that small.
- Merged upstream/main (#1395 rewrote `liveMove`). The merge keeps #1395's `rotaryFeedCap` and every #1395 refusal, as M3 resolved it in review.

title: fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates
body:
Replaces #951: the same commits, moved to a branch in this repository so the maintainer's agents can work it (maintainer's order, 2026-11-13). Still a draft, held for the PathPilot Hub run.

**Changes posted G-code: waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.**

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a). Effort: high (safety floor: posted G-code; no escalation).

## What changed
- **One shared rule** - `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` (new, appended to the prelude every `.cps` sees): `rotaryRate(letter)` (stated feed speed, else rapid, deg/min), `rotaryFeedCap(f, lin, turns, mode)`, `rotaryFeed(p, prev, letters, mode, arc)` and `rotaryFeedWord(v)`. It caps F so no rotary runs past its stated rate and no linear part past `feedRateMax`, read the way the control reads F:
  - **path** - `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` under G43.4. F is the tool tip's speed relative to the work, with the rotaries carried along (FANUC 30i-B operator's manual, tool center point control): F <= rate x tip / |d|. With the tip still, F <= the rate.
  - **composite** - `doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` C-axis live tooling (#860). The control times the block over sqrt(lin^2 + sum d^2), counting degrees as mm (FANUC 0i-F operator's manual, feedrate for rotation axes). `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
  - **Arcs** that turn a rotary use the path rule over the chord in the arc's plane. That chord is never longer than any reading of an arc's F, so the cap is never too loose.
- A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A cap under 0.1 mm/min is refused by name.
- The post now tracks the angles the control holds (`rotAt`), taken only from the A/B/C words it actually wrote. If a feed turns a rotary from an angle the post never wrote, and that rotary states a rate, the post refuses it by name: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held`. Each rate refusal is counted once per program.
- An unstated rate caps nothing (the unstated-limit law).
- `tormach.cps` needs no cap: it writes A only on a G0 index and refuses an A that changes inside an operation (#785). haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse every tilted record.
- The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/885-rotary-feed-cap.md`.

## How tested
New pinning suite `crates/app/tests/rotary_feed_cap.rs`. It reads every posted motion block back, keeps the axes modal, and checks every feed block that turns A against the stated rates under that dialect's reading:
- `fanuc_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (pins `A30 F3.3`, `A60 F1000` and the uncapped `A61 F2000`)
- `doosan_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate`
- `doosan_fourth_axis_composite_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (also pins the refusal when no A word was ever written)
- `an_unstated_rate_caps_nothing`
- `a_feed_turning_from_an_unknown_angle_is_refused_by_name`

The lathe stays pinned by `c_axis_unwind::a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` and its golden, which did not change.

Gate (local, macOS, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` plus the 44 post-touching binaries: all green, 377 tests. The binaries are arc_planes, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, comment_escape, conformance, control_comp, coolant_followups, doosan_dnm_post, drill_prior, drill_rplane, fanuc_post, fourth_axis_pose, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_equivalence/post/probe, lathe_*, machine_library, plasma_*, post_unit_word, probe_*, program_comments, program_entry, rotary_feed_cap, turning_face_approach, vertical_arc_entry, wear_comp, tilt, rotary_verify, tormach_fourth_axis, microarc_test_part, tormach_machines and posting.

`fourth_axis_pose.rs` `tilted()` now opens with a rapid at the pose before its two feeds. Under the new refusal, its feeds would otherwise turn the shipped DNM 5700's rated A from an angle the post never placed. The tests' own assertions are unchanged.

title: feat(post): Explain G-code option, explain() PRELUDE helper, manifest and refusal
body:
## What changed

Adds an opt-in **Explain G-code** post option, with the engine side designed on #1358.

- `PostOptions.explain` (default off). It is set per document or per setup through the existing undoable `SetPostOptions` / `SetSetupPostOptions` commands. `posting::options_value` publishes `postOptions.Explain = true` only when it is on. The project file writes an `explain` key (document and setup) only when it is on. With the option off, scripts and project files see exactly what they saw before.
- New `crates/post/src/post/explain.rs`. It holds the `explain(words)` JS helper, loaded after the PRELUDE, plus the manifest reading (`explains = "paren" | "semi"`, optional `commentMax` 8..=255, default 60).
  - The engine arms the helper only when the option is on. Unarmed, it returns `""`, so Explain-off output is byte-identical.
  - The helper strips `( ) ; %` and control characters, leads any active keyword with `- `, and cuts each comment to `commentMax`, cutting back to a whole meaning where it can.
  - Unknown G/M words are skipped, not guessed.
- With Explain on, a post whose manifest states no `explains` form (or an unknown one) is **refused by its name** before any hook runs. The refusal sits next to the #902 `programUnits` refusal (`units::post_name` is now shared).
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` documents the manifest keys. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1386-explain-option.md`.

title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
Stacked on #1181 (on #1163, #1144, #1139, #1123, #560, #551)

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.

title: feat(edm): wire EDM 4-axis - upper and lower profiles paired into rulings by a stated rule
body:
Stacked on #1163 (`issue/536-wire-taper` @ b14882ea, merged into this branch first). The wire base #1139, #1144, #1147 and #1160 are merged to main; #1150 and #1158 are pending. Merge order: #1163, then this PR. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A Wire Contour can now cut the ruled surface between two profiles given separately (#290 D2).

- **Op.** `WireContourOp.four_axis: Option<WireFourAxis>` (`pairing`, `sync`, `tolerance`); absent by default, omitted from the file when absent, so a one-profile cut's file, stamp, CL and NC are unchanged. The pairing rule has no default in the file. Edited through `EditOperationParams` / the MCP parameter patch (the same JSON door); the page shows the rule, the tolerance and the sync pairs as numbers.
- **Profiles.** The selection is read as two picks (a face's one outer ring, or a closed edge chain), each flat; the higher is the upper profile. Their heights must be the op's top and bottom planes (`app::operation::wire_ruled`).
- **Pairing** (`motion::wire_edm::pairing`). One monotone map between the two rings' arc lengths, fixed by anchors: by normalised arc length from each profile's point nearest the start hole, or by sync pairs with arc length between them. A ruling at every vertex of either ring; each move ends on a ruling's lower point, its pose the wire toward the upper point; upright at the start hole. The path's note states the rule.
- **Laws** (`motion::wire_edm::ruled_laws`). Fold: consecutive rulings whose ends run against each other (`a . b < 0` - the section turns back inside the part height). Crossing: the wire's section at a quarter height crosses itself. Ruled kerf: at 33 heights the wire's section stands off the stated surface by #1163's leaning-kerf reach `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)`.
- **A twisted ruled surface.** A straight wire cannot touch it along its whole height, so offsetting both profiles by the kerf gouges between the planes (about 12 um on a square-to-round corner with a 0.33 mm kerf). The generator widens the offset on both planes, uniformly, until the kerf stands clear at every height read, says in the notes how much stands on the profile planes, and refuses past the op's `tolerance` (default 0.05 mm). A constant taper needs exactly #1163's `1 / cos(angle)`.
- **Refused by name:** crossed sync points ("sync pair #3 crosses sync pair #2"), doubled, unpaired or off-profile sync points, a folding or self-crossing pairing, open profiles or one open and one closed, a ruling past `edm.max_taper_deg` (unstated refuses), a twist past the tolerance, profiles that are not two / not flat / not on the op's planes, a taper angle stated beside the two profiles, a lead whose leaning kerf enters the surface. The U/V stroke, U/V axes, guide planes and guide reach are #1163's machine check, unchanged (it reads poses).
- **Verify.** A 4-axis cut's poses are read as the wire's lean exactly as a stated taper's; kerf, threading and slug run at every judged height; a gouge blocks the post.
- **Post.** `PARAM WireFourAxis` (the rule's words) opens the section; `wire-iso.cps` writes the same `taper_on` / `uv` / `taper_off` codes from `edm.codes` as a tapered section and names the cut in a comment.

## Sources (Clean Room)

Piegl and Tiller, "The NURBS Book" (ruled surface between two parametrised curves, chord-length parametrisation); Farin, "Curves and Surfaces for CAGD"; do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces" (the tangent plane along a ruling of a non-developable ruled surface); Liu, "Five-axis NC cylindrical milling of sculptured surfaces", CAD 27(12), 1995. No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`.

## Refresh (2026-11-13: #1163's refresh merged in, then upstream main @ a5d1a763)

- Kept both sides (also `operation/types/mod.rs` against main's `SinkerPass` export): #1163's burnout, open-run clearance and sinker fields sit beside `four_axis` in the op, DTO, job, page and every `WireContourOp` test literal.
- A 4-axis cut with a no-core burnout is refused by name (the burnout is cut vertical only), like #1163's taper + burnout refusal. Open profiles and a left/right side stay refused by the ruled generator.
- Verify still reads a 4-axis cut's poses as the wire's lean, and the leaning kerf is judged at every height. The new `burnout` flag is carried through.
- Main's posted-golden law asks a gate to judge every posted golden. `crates/app/tests/posted_gates/wire_4axis.rs` regenerates `wire_4axis_punch.cl` (byte-identical) and judges it with `taper: true` against the loft's own mesh, sliced at 25 heights: no finding, and the punch frees the part (`solid_law_goldens::the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates`). No law was loosened.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/wire_4axis.rs`
  - `a_square_to_round_punch_posts_its_golden_and_verifies` - goldens `tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` (a pose on every move) and `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` (synthetic fixture); the wire clause reports no problem.
  - `a_constant_taper_by_sync_points_is_the_taper_golden_and_arc_length_differs` - the CL equals #1163's `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte, the NC equals `wire_taper_punch.nc` but for the comment naming the cut; arc length on the same two profiles gives other rulings.
  - `crossed_folded_and_unpaired_sync_points_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pairing_past_the_machine_or_off_the_planes_is_refused_by_name` (max taper at generation, U stroke at the post, one profile, taper + 4-axis, planes off the profiles)
  - `a_ruling_that_gouges_the_part_blocks_the_post`
  - `the_four_axis_block_round_trips_and_its_rule_is_never_defaulted` (JSON door, stamp, undo, the door's refusal of a NaN tolerance)
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_tests.rs` (8 tests): square-to-round keeps the kerf out and a zero tolerance refuses it; arc length vs sync points; the constant taper equals `wire_contour_tapered` move for move; crossed / folded / unpaired / off-profile / doubled sync points; open and mismatched profiles; steep rulings; a conical die.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/536-wire-taper` green on the final head 263442bc (motion lib, the whole app suite set - a new golden is shared test input - and the mapped ui suites; 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## What was not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture with invented codes.
- The die side at the app level (the motion crate pins a conical die); a die whose start hole is equidistant from several sides has no single nearest point - its arc-length seam is then the first tie, and a pairing that folds or twists for it is refused, not guessed.
- A model whose tessellated twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface of its two end profiles is refused by the wire laws as a gouge (the fixtures here are split along the inner diagonal). Follow-up #1170.
- Sync points are numbers on the page, not viewport picks (#1171). Fans and profiles stitched from several runs are refused by name (#1172). Open-profile 4-axis waits for #1109.
- UI: the new rows have no structural-test assertion of their own; no snapshot PNG was changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's DTO notes are not updated (a process file); the block rides `params` through the existing tools (#1108).

Changelog: Wire EDM 4-axis: a Wire Contour cuts the ruled surface between separately picked upper and lower profiles, paired by arc length or by sync points; crossed, folding or unpaired pairings, rulings past the machine's taper and U/V limits and a twist past the stated tolerance are refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation)

title: feat(edm): Wire Contour skim passes - per-pass condition, offset and direction
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Expected merges: retarget to `main` after #1139 merges. #1143 (Wire UI, also on #1139) touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs`; this PR changes one line there (the op destructure gains `..`), so a trivial conflict at most. #534 (verify) and #1109 (open profile) on #1123 are not touched.

## What changed

The Wire Contour gains skim passes: a rough pass, then N skims, each naming its own machine condition (and so its own offset, wire radius + that condition's gap), with an optional direction reversal per skim.

- `operation::WireContourOp.skims: Vec<WireSkim { condition, reverse }>`; file / MCP JSON `skims: [{ condition, reverse? }]`, absent when empty (rough-only files and goldens unchanged). Edits ride `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the existing MCP params door.
- Command door (`wire_op::condition_of`): every skim's condition resolved through #531's door, refused by name when it names none or the machine does not state it; then `motion::wire_edm::check_passes`: a pass nearer the profile than the finishing (last) pass ("would cut past the finished profile", rough included), a skim farther out than the pass before it ("would cut only air"), a skim condition with another wire diameter ("one threading cuts every pass with one wire").
- Generator: `motion::wire_edm::wire_passes` (new `skims.rs`) runs #532's single-pass generator per pass at its own offset, every law at that offset; each pass leads in from the threading point and back; a reversed skim walks clockwise. No skims is `wire_contour` exactly.
- Stamp digests each skim's condition numbers and direction (writes nothing for no skims - no stored stamp moves).
- Post stream (`posting_wire`): a mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition <skim id>` before each skim's first move (after each return to the threading point); a path that does not return once per pass is refused.
- `wire-iso.cps`: a condition that arrives with the wire threaded is the next skim's - `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `comp_off` again at its first move; the wire stays threaded.
- **Wire laws (#534) and skims** (merge with main, 2026-11-13): `sim::verify::wire` now judges each move at its own pass's kerf. Before this, every move was judged at the rough's kerf, which read skim 1 as a false 0.0200 mm gouge at move 8 (0.165 - 0.145). `WireJob.skim_offsets`, new `passes.rs`: the path is split at each return to the threading point, the threading law takes the widest pass, and the slug law sweeps each pass at its own offset. Skims on an open run are refused at the door and in the law. The arithmetic is in the decision record.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

## How tested

- New golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` (rough C110 + skim S21 + reversed skim S31 on #533's synthetic fixture): three distinct offsets (X-20.165 / -20.145 / -20.135), three condition selects, one thread, one cut.

title: feat(post): work offsets ride the stream as a 1-based index; the post writes the word
body:
Slice 1 of 3 for #931: the post crate and scripts. Stacked on #945 (#934, Sinumerik G505/G506). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

**This changes the post interface** (what every script receives as `PARAM WorkOffset`), so it waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.

## What changed

- **The stream carries the index.** `dump` writes `PARAM WorkOffset` as the setup's 1-based offset number (`G55` -> `2`). App still hands the word and still caps at 6; slice 2 makes the `Dump` field an index.
- **New `workOffsetIndex` manifest flag** (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs`, on the `coolantModes` pattern). It is read once at load with `workOffsetMax` (6 when unstated):
  - A flagged script receives the number. The engine refuses an offset above its maximum by setup name.
  - An unflagged (user) script receives the word `G54`..`G59` for 1-6, exactly as before. Any offset above 6 is refused by setup name, and an unflagged script cannot raise its own maximum.
  - The legacy words `G54`..`G59` in a stream still read as 1-6. Any other value (`G53`, 0, 2.5, `G54.1 P3`) is refused by setup name before a script sees it.
  - `work_offset::work_offsets(cps)` returns the maximum and the `workOffsetName(n)` names for slice 2's display. It never feeds the stream.
- **All 11 scripts shipped when this was written** declare the flag (grblhal.cps and tinyg.cps, added to main later, do not yet: they stay on the unflagged path, offsets 1-6, follow-up #1385), `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName`, and map the index to their own word. No `slotOf` / `frameWord` / `frameOf` word parsing remains:
  - The Fanuc-family probe register reads `wcsIndex - 1`.
  - Sinumerik's `$P_UIFR[n]` uses the number directly.
  - Heidenhain maps offset n to preset row n.
- **Declared maxima:**
  - Tormach mill and Tormach lathe: **9** (`G59.1`..`G59.3`, cited to the LinuxCNC G-code reference: "G54-G59.3 Select Coordinate System (1 - 9)" and its G10 L2 table).
  - Every other dialect: **6**. Haas G154, Fanuc/Mazak/Doosan G54.1 P and further Sinumerik/Heidenhain frames or rows were not verified against a public manual, so none is written. Reasons and sources are in `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-post.md`.
- **Docs.** `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents the 1-based `WorkOffset` beside the probe's 0-based `SetWorkOffset` (triage point 4). `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes the flag, the maximum and the name function.

## Tests

- New `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` (9 tests). Every shipped script runs on recorded streams at offsets 1, 6, 7, its maximum and one past it, checking the word it writes or the refusal by setup name. It also covers:
  - a recorded generator toolpath (`face_square_40x40.cl`) through Fanuc and Tormach;
  - legacy word streams posting byte-identically to their index;
  - invalid values;
  - an unflagged user script at 1-6 and at 7, and one that tries to raise its maximum;
  - a flagged script without a maximum or names;
  - the dump writing the index;
  - each script's name table.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame` now expects the engine's refusal of `G53` (the engine refuses it before the script runs).
- Gate (local, worktree target, sccache), on head `2fe7afb7`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
  - 63 app suites, 431 passed, 0 failed. They cover every app suite that posts through the shipped scripts: conformance, golden_cl, posting, arc_planes, cli, the probe_* suites, sinumerik_*, heidenhain_*, fanuc_post, doosan_dnm_post, carvera_*, tormach_*, the lathe_post* suites, plasma_*, inverted_*, comment_escape, one_wcs, setups, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, rotated_wcs, setup_mounts_post, setup_post_options, per_op_files, program_comments, smoothing, after_op, coolant*, post_unit_word, regression_models, wear_comp, control_comp and lathe_spindle_law. There are no separate mazak or haas suites; those scripts are covered by conformance, fanuc_post and the inverted_* suites.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- 400-line law: the new manifest reading lives in its own module, `work_offset.rs`. `engine.rs` (511 -> 530 lines) and `js.rs` (409 -> 415) were already over 400 and grew only by the hook-up.

**Goldens:** no golden file changed. Offsets 1-6 post the same words as before.

**Not exercised:** the GUI and MCP (unchanged in this slice), a real control, and offsets above 6 end to end through app (app still caps at 6 until slice 2).

title: fix(thread): a matched thread mill verifies clean - the gouge laws read its major circle
body:
#1071: a Thread op's helix runs the thread depth H = 0.5413 x pitch past the declared hole, which is the thread's minor circle (what CAD draws of a tapped hole), by design (`machining2d::thread_mill`). The verify read that hole as a wall the cutter must keep `r` from, so every matched thread mill was blocked.

That covered the stock source too, which the issue thought was unaffected: the same thread from `SrcRef::Stock` had 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs. `mill2d_c` never asserted the warnings, so no thread mill could post from any source.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a (head ea76d5df).

## What changed

Three laws convicted a matched thread, and each is fixed narrowly.

- **Law (b), the rim.** The Thread arm now moves each declared hole's rim out to the major circle (declared radius + H), after the region is built (`material_source::major_rims`). This covers every source and the area-controlled region. A loop that is the hole's minor rim (ours, or the model's own for a through hole) gives way to it; every other wall stays.
- **The containment solid law.** It read the model's minor wall, and the face the hole opens through, as part to keep. A new `sim::verify::thread_bore` (and `solid_hits_threaded`) excuses a hit only when both of these hold:
  - the facet is the thread's own material: the minor wall (near-vertical, every vertex on the declared circle within max(2 % r, 0.1 mm)), or a facet with a vertex on that circle lying wholly at or above the hole's entry (the mouth);
  - the swept cutter stays inside the major cylinder: the farther tip end's radius plus the atom's radius is at most the major radius plus the allowance.

  Floors, walls of another radius, other holes and any cut past the major circle still convict. `solid_hits` is unchanged: it calls the threaded form with no bores.

  **Since the review of f122474d:** the band only RECOGNISES the wall. The cap reads the hit facet's own radius about the axis (its nearest on-circle vertex) plus the thread depth plus the allowance, not the declared major circle. A hole declared wider than, or off the centre of, the model's hole by more than the allowance now convicts. `major_rims` likewise grows a through hole's major circle from the model's own rim loop when that stands nearer than the declared circle.
  **Since the review of 434a464a:** the wall is measured at the facet's (or rim loop's) nearest point to the axis, not its nearest vertex. A chord between two on-circle vertices dips inside the circle.
  - That nearest point must itself be on the band, so a D-bore's flat, a coarse polygon's side, or a step reaching inside the mouth is never the thread's material.
  - The wall stands at that point, credited at most `CHORD_CREDIT` (the sim's `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm) toward its nearest vertex. That is tessellation of a round hole: the STEP importer meshes at half of it.
  - `major_rims` reads the same way. It moved with `thread_bores` into `operation/thread_rims.rs`, so `material_source.rs` stays at main's 350 lines.
- **Law (a), crossings.** The retract runs the ride backwards at feed. The reversed arcs put their chord joints a last bit off their twins, and `proper_cross` excused a touch only at an exactly zero orientation. So each shared joint, and each collinear overlap, read as a crossing.

  Now chords that only touch (an endpoint within 1 nm of the other chord's line) are no crossing. A real crossing keeps every endpoint off the other line. This is the one change that reaches every operation's verify, so the whole batch tier was run (below). A parallel-only guard was tried first: it removed 5 of the 21 pairs, and the rest were the joint touches.
- Two functions now take eight arguments (`SolidIndex::hits`, `contain_into`). They carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` with a reason, as ten others in `sim` already do.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1071-thread-mill-rim.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs` (a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill, pitch 1, model-sourced unless named):
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_air_verifies_clean`: the issue's cavity fixture (#1073's block). Before the fix: 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs.

## What changed

`web/build-app-wasm.sh`: the `--config patch.crates-io...` build makes cargo rewrite the workspace `Cargo.lock` (flecs_ecs 0.2.2 / flecs_ecs_sys 0.2.1 lose `source` and `checksum`). The script now saves the tracked lock to `target/wasm-tools/Cargo.lock.keep` before its first cargo call (moved up from step 3, so `cargo fetch` and the wasm-bindgen install are covered too), and an `EXIT` trap restores it on success, failure and Ctrl-C/TERM. The header documents this; the only gap is SIGKILL, where the header says to run `git checkout -- Cargo.lock`.

Note: the main-branch script already had a restore trap on the cargo build step. The bug as filed reproduces only without it (a direct cargo call with the same `--config` dirties `Cargo.lock`). This PR moves the save/trap ahead of every cargo call and documents it.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/949-wasm-script-lock.md` (restore-from-copy chosen over a temp manifest dir).

## Readings (run in the worktree, `git status --short`)

- Before the change, direct cargo with the same `--config` patches: ` M Cargo.lock` (bug reproduced).
- Failed run, new script (wasm32 target not installed, so cargo fails after resolving): exit 101, `error[E0463]: can't find crate for core`; `git status --short` shows only the script edit, `Cargo.lock` clean.
- Interrupt check with the same save/restore shape and a 30 s step: lock dirty mid-run (` M Cargo.lock`), clean after SIGINT (EXIT trap runs on signal exit).

- A successful full wasm build: the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is not installed on the test machine, so the success path was not run. It uses the same EXIT trap, but this is unverified by a real success run.

title: fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates
body:
**Changes posted G-code: waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.**

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a). Effort: high (safety floor: posted G-code; no escalation).

## What changed
- **One shared rule** - `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` (new, appended to the prelude every `.cps` sees): `rotaryRate(letter)` (stated feed speed, else rapid, deg/min), `rotaryFeedCap(f, lin, turns, mode)`, `rotaryFeed(p, prev, letters, mode, arc)` and `rotaryFeedWord(v)`. It caps F so no rotary runs past its stated rate and no linear part past `feedRateMax`, read the way the control reads F:
  - **path** - `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` under G43.4. F is the tool tip's speed relative to the work, with the rotaries carried along (FANUC 30i-B operator's manual, tool center point control): F <= rate x tip / |d|. With the tip still, F <= the rate.
  - **composite** - `doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` C-axis live tooling (#860). The control times the block over sqrt(lin^2 + sum d^2), counting degrees as mm (FANUC 0i-F operator's manual, feedrate for rotation axes). `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
  - **Arcs** that turn a rotary use the path rule over the chord in the arc's plane. That chord is never longer than any reading of an arc's F, so the cap is never too loose.
- A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A cap under 0.1 mm/min is refused by name.
- The post now tracks the angles the control holds (`rotAt`), taken only from the A/B/C words it actually wrote. If a feed turns a rotary from an angle the post never wrote, and that rotary states a rate, the post refuses it by name: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held`. Each rate refusal is counted once per program.
- An unstated rate caps nothing (the unstated-limit law).
- `tormach.cps` needs no cap: it writes A only on a G0 index and refuses an A that changes inside an operation (#785). haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse every tilted record.
- The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/885-rotary-feed-cap.md`.

## How tested
New pinning suite `crates/app/tests/rotary_feed_cap.rs`. It reads every posted motion block back, keeps the axes modal, and checks every feed block that turns A against the stated rates under that dialect's reading:
- `fanuc_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (pins `A30 F3.3`, `A60 F1000` and the uncapped `A61 F2000`)
- `doosan_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate`
- `doosan_fourth_axis_composite_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (also pins the refusal when no A word was ever written)
- `an_unstated_rate_caps_nothing`
- `a_feed_turning_from_an_unknown_angle_is_refused_by_name`

The lathe stays pinned by `c_axis_unwind::a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` and its golden, which did not change.

Gate (local, macOS, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` plus the 44 post-touching binaries: all green, 377 tests. The binaries are arc_planes, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, comment_escape, conformance, control_comp, coolant_followups, doosan_dnm_post, drill_prior, drill_rplane, fanuc_post, fourth_axis_pose, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_equivalence/post/probe, lathe_*, machine_library, plasma_*, post_unit_word, probe_*, program_comments, program_entry, rotary_feed_cap, turning_face_approach, vertical_arc_entry, wear_comp, tilt, rotary_verify, tormach_fourth_axis, microarc_test_part, tormach_machines and posting.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
**None.** No committed golden states a rotary rate on a tilted feed. The lathe's C-axis goldens (`c_axis_unwind.nc`, `c_axis_helix.nc`) are byte-identical through the shared rule.

## Test fixture changed
`fourth_axis_pose.rs` `tilted()` now opens with a rapid at the pose before its two feeds. Under the new refusal, its feeds would otherwise turn the shipped DNM 5700's rated A from an angle the post never placed. The tests' own assertions are unchanged.

## Not exercised
- No Hub run or machine cut yet.
- G93 inverse time is not implemented (see the decision file).
- Under G43.4 the machine's linear axes also make a compensating move that depends on the pivot length. No machine file states that length, so the control's own per-axis clamp covers it. The post caps the tip at `feedRateMax`.

Found while working this: #950 (P0). doosan-dnm without TCP assumes A0 at program start and after a tool change, so an A0 section after an A30 section posts no A word. This PR does not fix that output. With a rated A, it now refuses such a feed by name.

Fixes #885

body:
## What changed

Phase 1 of #763: **`OpFrame`** — the one machining-frame seam in
`crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` — composes the two existing frame
mechanisms (the setup's `part_alignment` from #326 and the op's 3+2
`Tilt` from M5.1 B) behind one door, and `collect_job` reads through it:

- `OpFrame::of(op)` built once per generation; material and heights
  resolve through it; the tilt frame comes from
  `OpFrame::checked_frame` — one construction site, the refusal keeping
  its exact words and its exact precedence (after the heights resolve,
  the job's error-order law).
- The contract is stated once in the module header: D / S / L frames,
  right-to-left composition `p_L = T(A(p_D))`, the CL wrapping back via
  `TiltedFrame::world_path` (identity clone without a tilt), and the
  furniture law (stock / WCS / fixtures live in S: never aligned, but
  read local by the tilt).
- Heights and bounds in L ship correct from day one
  (`aabb_local_of`, `height_z_local`): they resolve against FULLY
  TRANSFORMED geometry, never a `z − origin.z` shift of the S box —
  the shift is only correct while the tool axis is the world Z.

**No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.** The four
verified kinds, picks, area controls and tilt-in-aligned-setups keep
their refusals; the later phases lift them one by one, each with its
numeric pin.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/opframe_seam.rs` (8 tests) + the seam's inline
  unit tests (6): identity passthrough; zero-tilt index reproduces the
  prismatic path EXACTLY move-for-move (the identity-bits law); a
  tilted face runs in its own plane (every endpoint maps back into the
  L1-folded height band over the local silhouette, tool axis =
  hand-computed Rx(45)); 90-degree alignment turns the solid and its
  TopOfModel height (15, not 10); 180-degree alignment mirrors the
  facets by hand math; alignment × tilt composition pinned against
  hand-composed transforms; local heights/boxes read fully transformed
  geometry (and provably NOT the z-shift); picks stay refused by name
  while the door Phase 2 will read through is already aligned.
- Capability gates: unchanged by design; the tilted-move refusal keeps
  its existing verbatim pin in `tests/inverted_post.rs`.
- The four kinds' aligned generation keeps its pins in the #326 suites
  (`plane_align`, `axis_align`, `rest_across_setups`, …), run by the
  same gate.

## What was not exercised

- The L-frame height/AABB resolve methods are pinned by tests only —
  no production call site switches onto them until Phase 2+ lifts the
  matching refusals (deliberate: the seam lands behavior-identical).
- The boundary/region builders (`boundary_ctx`, `material_region`,
  `boundary_picks`) still build their own frames from `op.params.tilt()`
  — they move onto the seam in the later phases.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

Quick gate (debug) on the final tree: 28 camcraft-app binaries, among them conformance 6 (goldens unchanged by the lift fix, their machine states safeRetractZ 0), grblhal_post 9, fanuc_post 11, after_op 10, coolant 7, machine 32 and posting 17, all green; camcraft-post `comp` 9/9; camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` 6/6 and `post` 19/19; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` clean. Whole-crate `clippy --tests` stops on the pre-existing `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` compile error (missing field `hand`), which is on upstream main and not touched here.

## Review fix (smoothing, head 6129a904)

With per-operation smoothing (#616) on, the post writes one `(SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - GRBLHAL STATES NO SMOOTHING TOLERANCE)` note per program (grblHAL lists G61 only, no tolerance word) and resets the ask per section. Pinned by `smoothing::fanuc_and_mazak_name_the_ask_once_and_write_no_unbounded_word` (now covers grblHAL). Goldens unchanged (smoothing off).

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a real grblHAL controller or its simulator - testers welcome.** Anyone with a grblHAL machine: please post a program with this post, dry-run it (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold), and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`.

Changelog: grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill) and a generic grblHAL 3-axis machine; G41/G42, G84, probing and go-home are refused by name; a smoothing ask is named once, never written unbounded

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

## How tested
- motion `turning_thread_infeed`, 10/10, including two new tests:
  - every roughing depth is cut twice (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.2) and the default is unchanged move for move;
  - a repeat is the same pass under every method × schedule, and the verdict stays silent.
- app:
  - `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5: the toggle goes stale and back to OK, takes 3 then 5 plunges, with undo and redo; round-trip writes the key only when set;
  - `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 5/5: G76 refuses the repeat; `REP 1` rides the stream; G32 posts 5 passes.
- `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `inverted_post`, `project_roundtrip` and the app lib pass. No golden changed.
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on cl, post, motion, app and ui is clean.
- The only failure is the headless-GPU ui test (no adapter on this Mac).

## Not exercised (draft)
GUI check and a lathe sim or machine run. There is a combined test kit for #416, #417 and #418.
